questions.solution:

questions.text: Match the following according to input (from the left column) to the complier phase (in the right column) that processes it.
questions.solution:

questions.text:
Consider the expression ( a-1)* (((b + c) / 3) + d)) . Let X be the minimum number of
registers required by an optimal code generation (without any register spill) algorithm for a
load/store architecture in which (i) only loads and store instructions can have memory
operands and (ii) arithmetic instructions can have only register or immediate operands. The
value of X is _________.
questions.solution:
Evaluate the bigger subtree first:
- R1 = b, R2 = c, R1 = R1 + R2, R1 = R1 / 3, R2 = d, R1 = R1 + R2
- R2 = a, R2 = R2 [latex]-[/latex] 1, R1 = R2 * R1

Only 2 registers are ever needed.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar:

stmt[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] if expr then expr else expr; stmt| [latex]\dot{O}[/latex]
expr[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]term relop term|term
term[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] id|number
if[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]a|b|c
number[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [0-9]

where relop is a relational operate (e.g [latex]\lt ,\gt[/latex],...), [latex]\dot{O}[/latex] refers to the empty statement, and if ,then, else are terminals.

Consider a program P following the above grammar containing ten if terminals. The number of control flows paths in P is ____________. For example the program

if [latex]e_1[/latex] then [latex]e_2[/latex] else [latex]e_3[/latex]

has 2 controls flow paths [latex]e_{1} \rightarrow e_{2}[/latex] and [latex]e_{1} \rightarrow e_{3}[/latex].
questions.solution:
A program is a sequence of if-then-else statements. Each one has 2 possible branches, and the choices are independent.

With 10 of them: [latex]2^{10}=1024[/latex] control flow paths.

Answer: 1024

questions.text:
Consider the following intermediate program in three address code
p= a -b
q= p *c
p= u * v
q= p + q
Which one of the following corresponds to a static single assignment form of the above code?
questions.solution:
In SSA every variable is assigned exactly once, and each use refers to the latest version. Option 2: [latex]p_3=a-b[/latex], [latex]q_4=p_3c[/latex], [latex]p_4=uv[/latex], [latex]q_3=p_4+q_4[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] all distinct names with correct uses (the numbers themselves do not matter).

Option 1 reassigns [latex]p_1[/latex] and [latex]q_1[/latex]; option 3 uses undefined names; option 4 uses plain p and q.

Answer: Option 2
